title: BREST-OD-300 lead-cooled fast reactor with closed fuel cycle

research.what: A lead-cooled fast reactor with on-site mixed nitride uranium-plutonium fuel fabrication and reprocessing, developed by NIKIET under Rosatom's Proryv (Breakthrough) project. Origin: NIKIET BREST fast-reactor design (1990s) and Rosatom's 'Proryv' project (c. 2011); year approximate.

change.what: Rosatom has said physical start-up is planned for 2026-2027, with grid connection stated as the first half of 2027 in earlier statements and 2028 in a later one, at the Siberian Chemical Combine in Seversk.

note: It would be the first Generation IV reactor energy complex with a closed fuel cycle; the schedule has repeatedly moved and sanctions are cited as a difficulty.

title: First commercial natural (geologic) hydrogen production

research.what: Exploiting hydrogen that forms naturally underground and collects in reservoirs, rather than manufacturing it, following the first known commercial use in Mali. Origin: Bourakébougou well in Mali, the first known commercial use of naturally occurring hydrogen (drilled c. 2012, as described in the Oxford Institute for Energy Studies paper and the EFI Foundation report).

change.what: French developer FDE targets independent resource certification in 2027 and first commercial production in late 2028 in Lorraine, subject to permits; Mantle8 also aims to make natural hydrogen a reality by 2028.

note: Targets are company projections; commentators note that no engineered or natural subsurface hydrogen project has yet reached commercial production at scale.

title: West-to-East pure hydrogen pipeline (Ulanqab to Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei)

research.what: Transporting pure hydrogen over long distances by dedicated steel pipeline, building on short industrial hydrogen pipelines in China. Origin: Sinopec's earlier short pure-hydrogen industrial pipelines (for example Jiyuan–Luoyang, 2015). This origin is from general knowledge and is not confirmed in the cited pages.

change.what: Sinopec's roughly 1,145 km Ulanqab to Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei pipeline demonstration is planned to be built and put into operation in December 2027, starting at 100,000 tonnes of hydrogen a year.

note: It would be China's first long-distance, cross-provincial pure-hydrogen pipeline, linking green hydrogen from Inner Mongolia to refineries in the east.

refs.label: Solarbe: three pure-hydrogen pipelines to start construction (Chinese)
Sohu: 2025 hydrogen pipeline progress, safety review passed (Chinese)

security.note: It adds a networked, remotely monitored pipeline with SCADA and control systems, which become an operational technology target.

title: First phone NPU: Huawei Kirin 970 (Cambricon IP)

research.what: A Chinese Academy of Sciences team built a dedicated deep-learning processor architecture, which won a top architecture-conference best paper award. Origin: Cambricon / CAS Institute of Computing Technology deep-learning processor (2013 work, ASPLOS best paper)

change.what: Huawei launched the Kirin 970 phone chip with a dedicated neural processing unit built on Cambricon IP, and shipped it at scale in the Mate 10.

note: It put a dedicated neural accelerator into a mass-market phone SoC and started on-device AI as a standard phone chip block.

refs.label: PingWest: how the Kirin 970 phone AI chip came about
ScienceNet: Can China lead the AI chip ecosystem

security.note: Local neural processing moves sensitive data handling and models onto handsets, creating new on-device model and firmware attack targets.

title: WASI 1.0 and Component Model 1.0 stable standards

research.what: WASI defines a standard system interface for WebAssembly outside the browser. The Component Model adds language-neutral interfaces so modules written in different languages can be composed. Origin: The WASI system interface for WebAssembly, first published as 'preview1' in about 2019. It became WASI 0.2 with the Component Model in January 2024 and WASI 0.3 with native async in June 2026, under the Bytecode Alliance and the W3C WebAssembly WASI subgroup.

change.what: The WASI roadmap plans two-monthly 0.3.x releases through 2027, and WASI 1.0 may be scheduled outside that cycle. Other coverage expects 1.0 in late 2026 or early 2027. 1.0 depends on the Component Model reaching 1.0 first.

note: A 1.0 release would give a stable, portable server-side and edge runtime interface with compatibility guarantees. No firm 1.0 date has been published.

refs.label: WASI.dev Roadmap (release schedule through 2027)
Uno Platform: The State of WebAssembly 2025 and 2026
Bytecode Alliance: The Road to Component Model 1.0 (draft blog PR, Apr 2026)

security.note: Capability-based, sandboxed components could reduce supply-chain risk, but a wider ecosystem of third-party components also adds packaging and dependency risk.

title: Korea's Independent AI Foundation Model programme (독자 AI 파운데이션 모델)

research.what: Korea's science ministry funds competing elite teams (Naver, Upstage, SK Telecom, NC AI, LG AI Research) to build foundation models designed and trained wholly in Korea, with GPUs, data and talent support. Origin: MSIT 'Independent AI Foundation Model' project, announced 20 June 2025 (formerly called World Best LLM)

change.what: The programme runs in six-month competitive evaluation rounds through 2027. It targets about 95% of the performance of leading global models, with open-source release to spread them into public and commercial services.

note: It is a state-backed route to nationally owned LLMs deployed in public and commercial services, with staged milestones through 2027.

title: SpinQ Gemini desktop NMR quantum computer (双子座)

research.what: Room-temperature nuclear-magnetic-resonance quantum computing in a spin-qubit lab at Shenzhen was turned into a small permanent-magnet two-qubit machine for teaching. Origin: Spin Quantum Computing Laboratory, founded Sept 2017 at SUSTech / Shenzhen Institute for Quantum Science and Engineering / Peng Cheng Laboratory (NMR and ODMR platforms)

change.what: Shenzhen SpinQ (量旋科技) launched Gemini in January 2020, billed as the first commercially available desktop quantum computer, and sold it to universities.

note: It put a real, maintenance-free quantum processor into classrooms at a price universities could afford, opening a quantum-education hardware market.

title: On-device AI detection of fake voices in calls (LG U+ ixi-O)

research.what: Anti-spoofing models that tell synthetic or altered voices from real ones, shrunk enough to run on a phone, so the call audio never leaves the device. Origin: LG Uplus in-house Anti-DeepVoice work with LG AI Research (voice activity detection, speech-to-text and anti-spoofing, trained on about 3,000 hours of call data), first shown at MWC in March 2025

change.what: LG Uplus released Anti-DeepVoice in its ixi-O AI call app on 30 June 2025. It flags forged voices within about 5 seconds, and the company says it is the first on-device commercial release of the technology.

note: It moves defence against AI voice-cloning phone fraud onto the handset, so no call data has to be uploaded to a server.

title: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) for 6G coverage

research.what: Programmable metasurfaces that steer radio waves passively or semi-actively to extend and shape wireless coverage. They grew out of Chinese information-metamaterial research and theoretical RIS work from 2014 onward. Origin: Southeast University information-metamaterials team (Cui Tiejun) with China Mobile, whose 2021 Nanjing field trial of a tunable RIS followed the 2020 IMT-2030 (6G) Promotion Group RIS task force.

change.what: RIS is a listed key 6G technology within China's IMT-2030 programme, which is in its second trial stage (2026–2027). The first commercial 6G systems are expected around 2030, which is when RIS is expected to see real network use, with scaled deployment around 2035.

note: RIS is on China's 6G standardisation and trial roadmap. It is a coverage-enhancement component, not the whole of 6G.

refs.label: Sanpijiang report: 6G definition, key technologies, timeline (RIS, 2030 commercial launch)
2026 Global 6G Technology and Industry Ecosystem Conference: RIS standardisation and industrialisation
Sina Tech: China Mobile and Cui Tiejun's team complete RIS trial

security.note: Programmable surfaces in the radio path add a new controllable element that attackers could misconfigure or spoof, so they need authenticated control channels.

title: Proba-3: artificial solar eclipse by formation flying

research.what: Two ESA spacecraft flying in precise formation about 150 m apart so that one blocks the Sun for the other, forming a space-based coronagraph. Origin: ESA Proba-3 precision formation-flying mission with the ASPIICS coronagraph (Centre Spatial de Liège); described as a planned mission in a 2017 literature review

change.what: In June 2025 ESA released the first images of the solar corona taken during an artificial total eclipse created autonomously in orbit.

note: First demonstration of autonomous millimetre-class formation flying used to make an on-demand eclipse for science, with a hold time of up to 6 hours per orbit.

refs.label: ESA France – Première éclipse solaire artificielle de Proba-3
RTBF – Proba-3 : une première éclipse artificielle pour observer la couronne du soleil

security.note: Autonomous formation control without ground intervention adds a software-dependent spacecraft control chain that would need protecting against tampering.

title: Fission Surface Power: nuclear reactor on the Moon by 2030

research.what: NASA and the US Department of Energy have developed small space fission reactors, including the Fission Surface Power project begun in 2018, to supply continuous power through the two-week lunar night. Origin: NASA's Fission Surface Power Project (from 2018), which led to three 40 kW design contracts in 2022 and the 2025 NASA–DOE agreement.

change.what: NASA and DOE aim to have a lunar surface fission reactor, now with a target of at least 100 kW, ready for launch by 2030. A separate US directive also asks for a reactor that powers a spacecraft's electric thrusters.

note: Continuous power is needed for long-term lunar bases and for extracting resources. The schedule has been accelerated and carries technical and fuelling risk.

title: NAVER 1784: cloud-brained 'brainless' robots at work

research.what: NAVER LABS developed a cloud-based multi-robot intelligence system (ARC: AI, Robot, Cloud) in which robots carry no onboard 'brain' and are controlled over low-latency 5G. Origin: NAVER LABS ARC (AI·Robot·Cloud) brainless-robot / 5G cloud control research, around 2019 (year approximate, not stated in the cited pages)

change.what: In 2022 NAVER opened its robot-friendly 1784 headquarters, where about 100 'Rookie' brainless robots deliver parcels, lunch boxes and coffee, using a robot-only elevator and a private 5G network.

note: First large-scale building where a cloud 'brain' runs roughly a hundred service robots in daily office work, later offered as a commercial robot-cloud service.

title: Baloxavir (Xofluza): single-dose cap-endonuclease flu drug

research.what: Shionogi created an influenza antiviral that blocks the virus's cap-dependent endonuclease, a different mechanism from neuraminidase inhibitors such as Tamiflu. Origin: Shionogi (Osaka) in-house discovery of S-033188 (baloxavir marboxil); designated for Japan's Sakigake fast-track review in October 2015 (the discovery itself started earlier).

change.what: Japan approved it on 23 Feb 2018 and Shionogi launched it on 14 Mar 2018, the first flu treatment completed with one tablet dose.

note: First new-mechanism flu antiviral in years, developed in Japan and launched there first.

title: Room-temperature artificial red blood cells (Nara)

research.what: Nara Medical University developed a stockpilable artificial red-cell product that wraps haemoglobin in an artificial membrane, stays stable at room temperature for about two years and needs no blood-type matching. Origin: Nara Medical University (Prof. Hiromi Sakai) research group, supported by AMED from around 2015

change.what: Nara Medical University and partners aim for practical use and insurance coverage around 2030, after investigator-led trials that started in 2025.

note: It could give emergency, remote-island and disaster medicine a blood substitute that does not depend on donations.

title: Fully autonomous wind-blade inspection and repair robots (LEBO)

research.what: A Japanese startup built blade-crawling inspection and repair robots, paired with AI analysis of camera and drone images, to plan maintenance for each wind turbine. Origin: LEBO ROBOTICS Inc., a Japanese startup founded in 2018, which developed its own wind-turbine maintenance robots

change.what: Repair robots now run by a ground operator by remote control are expected to become fully autonomous within a few years of the August 2025 article, so around 2027-2028.

note: It would move wind-blade maintenance from remote-controlled robots to AI-planned work that runs without an operator.

title: AI-run O&M for remote renewable and grid stations

research.what: Combines large models, voiceprint detection, remote sensing, robots and smart wearables to monitor equipment and surroundings at stations in remote or harsh areas. Origin: NDRC/NEA 'AI+ Energy' Implementation Opinions (国能发科技〔2025〕73号), remote-station O&M task

change.what: China's plan sets AI-enabled intelligent O&M for stations in remote areas as an application scenario to be piloted under the 2027 and 2030 targets, supporting desert and offshore renewable bases.

note: The sources describe the scenario and the remote-base context, but no named deployment date or operator beyond the plan's 2027/2030 phases.

research.what: A French consortium (advizeo, Métropole du Grand Paris, Tilt) is developing AI that automates energy monitoring across about 7,000 public buildings. Origin: IA Eco-Pilot demonstrator, one of 8 winners of a French call for AI projects for the energy transition of territories, 2024

change.what: If the demonstrator succeeds, remote AI control of buildings combined with a flexibility offer is to be deployed more widely in the coming years. The 2028 date is my estimate, not a date stated in the sources.

title: AI Digital Convergence Platform for a fusion pilot plant

research.what: The Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory is building a fusion foundation model, a digital twin of the NSTX-U experiment and an AI computing infrastructure called STELLAR-AI to speed fusion pilot-plant development. Origin: Genesis Mission fusion work at PPPL (2025): NSTX-U digital twin, a fusion foundation model and STELLAR-AI

change.what: The DOE's Genesis Mission frameworks report ties AI-guided fusion engineering to a national milestone of an operational US fusion pilot plant on the grid between 2030 and 2035.

note: It treats whole-facility AI design and simulation as a way to shorten the fusion innovation cycle, which is separate from AI plasma control; 2030 is the start of the stated pilot-plant window.

title: Envision Galileo AI turbine with Tianji/Tianshu models

research.what: Envision built an energy-specific weather foundation model and a wind, solar, storage and power-market energy model, and fed live turbine data back into the weather model to improve forecasts. Origin: Envision Energy's in-house AI forecasting programme, which ranked first in China Southern Grid's power and load forecasting contests in 2022–2024.

change.what: In October 2025 Envision launched the Galileo AI wind turbine, which runs on its Tianji weather model and Tianshu energy model, after a demonstration wind farm had fitted the Tianshu control module to half its turbines since 2024.

note: It is a field-tested case of AI foundation models used for energy-asset design, control and forecasting. The company reports a revenue gain of about 20.9% against unmodified turbines at the same farm.

title: Power-industry cybersecurity large model (CEPRI, China)

research.what: A power-sector cybersecurity model was fine-tuned from the State Grid Guangming power large model on ten kinds of grid security corpora, and paired with the GridGraph power graph database to curb hallucination. Origin: China Electric Power Research Institute 'cybersecurity professional AI application' special research programme, built on the State Grid Guangming Power Large Model (released December 2024)

change.what: In May 2025 CEPRI reported that the first power-industry cybersecurity large model was in live use; its intelligence-analysis, vulnerability-verification and attack/defence Q&A agents supported grid protection during the Asian Winter Games and the national 'Two Sessions'.

note: It is a reported first sector-specific LLM security assistant for the grid, with stated gains: intelligence analysis cut from 1-2 days to half an hour, and vulnerability-check accuracy up an average of 25%.

title: EU Network Code on Cybersecurity: first grid-wide cyber risk cycle

research.what: ENTSO-E, the EU DSO Entity and ACER drafted a sector-specific code for cyber-security risk assessment, minimum and advanced controls, and incident reporting for cross-border electricity flows. Origin: Network code on cybersecurity mandated by the Electricity Regulation (EU) 2019/943 and drafted by ENTSO-E/EU DSO Entity with ACER (2019–2022), adopted as Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1366

change.what: After the Union-wide report due December 2026, Member State-level risk assessments follow by mid-2029 and designated high- and critical-impact entities must then apply the controls, which in practice reaches real-world use in 2027–2031.

note: This is the EU's first sector-specific cyber rulebook for electricity, and it is the compliance baseline for any AI-enabled or automated grid operations. Sources do not describe AI-specific requirements.

title: Kepler: first commercial optical data relay constellation

research.what: Kepler shifted to laser-based optical data relay, validating space-to-space, space-to-ground and space-to-air laser links and aligning with Space Development Agency optical standards. Origin: Kepler Communications optical relay programme and SDA-compatible optical inter-satellite link demonstrations (strategy shift announced 2024)

change.what: Kepler launched the first ten satellites of its optical relay network on 11 January 2026, starting the first commercial optical data relay constellation with on-orbit compute and hosted payloads.

note: It moves laser inter-satellite relay from demonstrations to a commercial network, with service due in 2026.

title: Computer passwords (MIT CTSS)

research.what: MIT's time-sharing project needed a way to give each user private files on a shared computer, so it gave each user a login and password. Origin: Compatible Time-Sharing System (CTSS) at the MIT Computation Center, led by Fernando Corbató, first demonstrated November 1961; described in Corbató et al., 'An Experimental Time-Sharing System' (1962)

change.what: CTSS is credited as the first computer system to use password login, and it ran for multiple users at MIT and at remote sites.

note: The per-user password became the basic way computers check who is using them, and the first password-file leak (1962) was an early security incident.

title: Hardware protection rings (Multics)

research.what: Robert Graham proposed nested rings of privilege, so that code in outer rings cannot touch more protected inner rings, as part of the Multics design. Origin: Graham's 1967 proposal for protection rings in Multics (MIT Project MAC); later hardware design by Schroeder and Saltzer, 'A hardware architecture for implementing protection rings' (1971/1972)

change.what: Multics, developed in the 1960s, is widely seen as the first operating system with protection rings, and Hitachi built a hardware ring system on the HITAC 5020E in 1968.

note: Ring-based privilege separation became the model for the kernel and user modes found in mainstream processors and operating systems.

title: Cyclotron radioisotopes for medicine (1936 first therapy)

research.what: Lawrence and Livingston built the first cyclotron in 1930, a magnetic resonance accelerator that later produced artificial radioactive isotopes. Origin: Lawrence and Livingston, first cyclotron, University of California Berkeley, 1930; 1932 paper on ions above 1 MeV

change.what: John Lawrence used cyclotron-made radioactive phosphorus to treat a leukaemia patient in 1936, the first therapeutic use of a cyclotron isotope, which started nuclear medicine.

note: Opened the way to radiotracers and radioisotope therapy, which are now routine in diagnosis and cancer treatment.

refs.label: Berkeley Lab: Physics Meets Biology

security.note: Little direct cyber relevance; modern medical cyclotron facilities use networked control systems.
